questions.stem: The destroyers (with distance \(d(t) = 10\sqrt{1300-450t+39t^2}\) km, starting at 9 a.m.) are "on alert" when they are less than \(40\) km apart. During what times will the two destroyers be "on alert"?

steps.explain: Set up the inequality \(d(t) < 40\), then square both sides to remove the square root (valid since both sides are positive).
Rearrange into standard quadratic-inequality form.
Find the boundary times by solving the corresponding equation with the quadratic formula. The discriminant is \(450^2-4(39)(1284)=202500-200304=2196\).
Evaluate both roots — these are the boundary times (in hours after 9 a.m.) between which the quadratic is negative (since it opens upward, it's negative BETWEEN the roots).
Convert these decimal hours after 9:00 a.m. into clock times: \(0.17h\approx10\)min, \(0.37h\approx22\)min.

topics.title: Using graphs to solve equations and inequations

questions.stem: The graph below shows the income and cost lines for a small business, in dollars, against the number of boxes sold. Use the graph to determine the number of boxes that need to be sold to break even.
questions.hint: The break-even point is where the Income line and the Cost line meet — the business earns exactly what it spent.

steps.explain: Breaking even means Income = Cost, i.e. the point where the two lines intersect on the graph.
Reading the graph, the Income and Cost lines cross at the point \((3, 15)\), i.e. after 3 boxes are sold both lines give \$15.
The \(x\)-coordinate of the intersection is the number of boxes.
steps.work: \(\therefore\) 3 boxes need to be sold to break even.

questions.stem: Why does \(\sin x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\) have three solutions?
options: The line is tangent to sine three times
Sine always has three roots on \([0, 2\pi]\)
The line only meets sine for \(x > 0\)
The line \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\) intersects \(y = \sin x\) at exactly three points

steps.explain: The equation \(\sin x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\) is equivalent to finding where the curve \(y = \sin x\) meets the straight line \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: The line has \(y\)-intercept \(1\) (so it starts at the same height as a maximum of sine) and a gentle negative slope of \(-\dfrac{1}{4}\).

Because the line decreases slowly, it can cross the oscillating sine curve more than once: typically once on the way down from the first peak, again later, and once more before the line drops below \(-1\).
On the standard domain shown in the exam diagram, the line intersects \(y = \sin x\) at exactly three points. That is why the equation has three solutions.

questions.stem: Approximate the largest solution of \(\sin x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\).

steps.explain: To solve the equation, we can find the intersection points of the graphs \(y = \sin x\) and \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{4}\). We want the largest of these \(x\)-values.
The line eventually falls below the range of sine (below \(-1\)), so only finitely many intersections exist. The last one occurs before the line drops too low.
Visually, the rightmost crossing lies a little to the left of \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) on a typical sketch.
Reading the graph carefully gives an approximate largest solution \(x \approx 5.8\).

questions.stem: Why does \(\cos x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\) have three solutions?
options: The line \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\) intersects \(y = \cos x\) at exactly three points

steps.explain: Rewrite \(\cos x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\) as intersections of \(y = \cos x\) and the line \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: The line passes through \((0, 1)\) (a maximum of cosine) with slope \(-\dfrac{1}{5}\), so it decreases even more slowly than a slope of \(-\dfrac{1}{4}\).
A slowly decreasing line starting at a cosine peak will cross the cosine wave several times before leaving the strip \([-1, 1]\).
On the diagram used in the exam, there are exactly three intersection points, so the equation has three solutions.

questions.stem: Approximate the largest solution of \(\cos x = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\).

steps.explain: The largest solution is the rightmost intersection of \(y = \cos x\) and \(y = 1 - \dfrac{x}{5}\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: Because the slope is only \(-\dfrac{1}{5}\), the line stays inside \([-1,1]\) a little longer than the previous similar problem.
From the graph, the final crossing is a little past \(2\pi\).
A reasonable approximation is \(x \approx 6.5\).

questions.stem: By drawing graphs on the number plane, show how many solutions exist for the equation \(\cos x = \left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right|\) in the domain \((-\infty,\infty)\).

steps.explain: Sketch \(y=\cos x\), which oscillates forever between \(-1\) and \(1\), and \(y=\left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right|\), a V-shaped graph with vertex at \((\pi,0)\), gradient magnitude \(\dfrac14\) on each side.
steps.work: \(\cos x\): amplitude 1, period \(2\pi\). \(\left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right|\): V-shape, vertex \((\pi,0)\), slope \(\pm\tfrac14\)

steps.explain: Since \(\cos x\) is bounded between \(-1\) and \(1\), intersections can only occur where the V-graph's height is also within \([-1,1]\) — i.e. where \(\left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right| \le 1\), which is \(\pi-4 \le x \le \pi+4\), a limited window.
steps.work: Intersections confined to \(x \in [\pi-4, \pi+4]\) (beyond this, the V-graph exceeds cosine's range)

steps.explain: Within that window, the V-graph crosses each hump/trough of the oscillating cosine curve — counting the crossings on the sketch (as shown above) gives the total number of solutions.
steps.work: Counting crossings on the graph: 4 intersection points visible

steps.explain: State the final count.
steps.work: \(\therefore\) there are 4 solutions to the equation.

questions.stem: Point \((-1, 3)\) on \(y = f(x)\) maps under \(y = -2f(x)\) to which point, with which transforms?
options: \((-1, -6)\); reflect in \(x\)-axis then vertical stretch by 2

steps.explain: The transformed graph is \(y = -2f(x)\). In coordinates, every point \((x, y)\) on the original graph is sent to \((x, -2y)\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: The factor \(-1\) reflects the graph in the \(x\)-axis. The factor \(2\) then stretches it vertically by a factor of \(2\) (distances from the \(x\)-axis double).
Apply this to the marked point: \((-1, 3) \mapsto (-1, -2 \times 3) = (-1, -6)\).
So the image of \((-1, 3)\) is \((-1, -6)\), and the whole curve is an inverted, vertically stretched copy of \(f\).

questions.stem: The function \( y=(x-2)^3-2 \) is translated 5 units to the right and 4 units up. Find the equation of the transformed curve.

steps.explain: A translation of \( h \) units right replaces \( x \) with \( x-h \) in the equation.
Simplify the bracket.
A translation of \( k \) units up adds \( k \) to the whole right-hand side.
Combine the constants to state the final transformed equation.

questions.stem: Which diagram best shows the graph of the parabola \(y = 2-(x+1)^2\)?
options: A downward-opening parabola with vertex \((-1,2)\), as shown above
questions.hint: Compare to \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\): the sign of \(a\) determines the direction it opens, and \((h,k)\) is the vertex.

steps.explain: Since \(a=-1<0\), the parabola opens downward. The vertex is at \((h,k) = (-1,2)\).
This matches the graph shown, with the maximum point at \((-1,2)\).

questions.stem: Point \((-1, 3)\) on \(y = f(x)\) maps under \(y = f\!\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + 2\right)\) to:

steps.explain: We want the image of the point \((-1, 3)\) under \(y = f\!\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + 2\right)\). The \(y\)-coordinate of a point on \(y = f(\ldots)\) equals \(f(\text{input})\), so we need the input to equal the original \(x\)-coordinate \(-1\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: Solve for the new \(x\): \(\dfrac{x}{2} = -3\), so \(x = -6\).
The \(y\)-value is unchanged because we still evaluate \(f\) at the same number \(-1\): \(y = f(-1) = 3\).
Geometrically this is a horizontal dilation by factor \(2\) followed by a translation \(4\) units left. The image point is \((-6, 3)\).

questions.stem: The figure shows the graph of \(y=f(x)\), meeting the \(x\)-axis at \((-3,0)\) and the \(y\)-axis at \((0,2)\), with a maximum at \((3,4)\), a minimum at \((-3,0)\), and a horizontal asymptote \(y=2\). What is the range of \(\frac{1}{2}f(x)\)?

steps.explain: From the graph, the curve's overall lowest value is its minimum, \(0\), and its overall highest value is its maximum, \(4\) — the asymptote \(y=2\) is a value the curve approaches but does not exceed further than the maximum already does.

steps.explain: The transformation \(\frac{1}{2}f(x)\) is a vertical dilation by factor \(\frac{1}{2}\) — it multiplies every \(y\)-value (and hence both range endpoints) by \(\frac{1}{2}\).
Evaluate.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of \(g(x) = f(3x) - 2\), labelling all points and asymptotes.

steps.explain: The transformation \(f(3x)\) is a HORIZONTAL dilation by factor \(\frac{1}{3}\) — every \(x\)-coordinate of the original points and asymptote-related features is divided by 3 (the \(y\)-values are unchanged).

questions.stem: How many solutions does \(\cos \pi x = 1 - |x|\) have for all real \(x\)?

steps.explain: Count intersections of \(y = \cos \pi x\) and \(y = 1 - |x|\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: Cosine stays in \([-1, 1]\). The V-shape \(1 - |x|\) drops below \(-1\) when \(|x| > 2\), so no intersections exist outside \([-2, 2]\).
On \([-2, 2]\), period-\(2\) cosine meets the inverted-V five times.
Hence the equation has 5 real solutions.

questions.stem: How many solutions does \(\sin \pi x = 1 - |x|\) have for all real \(x\)?

steps.explain: Count intersections of \(y = \sin \pi x\) and \(y = 1 - |x|\).
steps.work: We are asked to evaluate the expression step-by-step. First, identify the operations and any necessary common denominators or conversion method.

steps.explain: Sine has period \(2\) and range \([-1,1]\). The inverted-V peaks at \((0,1)\) and is below \(-1\) for \(|x| > 2\).
Unlike cosine (which has a peak at each even integer), sine is zero at integers. The sketches meet at the origin and at two symmetric side points only.
Therefore there are 3 real solutions.

questions.stem: The graph of \( g(x) = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \) is shown below, for \( -2\pi \le x \le 2\pi \). Which statement about the graph is correct?
options: The amplitude is 2, the period is \( 4\pi \), and the y-intercept is 1
The amplitude is 2, the period is \( \pi \), and the y-intercept is 1
The amplitude is 2, the period is \( 4\pi \), and the y-intercept is 2
The amplitude is \( \tfrac12 \), the period is \( 4\pi \), and the y-intercept is 1

steps.explain: For \( y = a\cos(bx+c) \), the amplitude is \( |a| \). Here \( a = 2 \).
The period is \( \dfrac{2\pi}{b} \), where \( b \) is the coefficient of \( x \) — here \( b = \tfrac12 \).
Find the y-intercept by substituting \( x = 0 \) into \( g(x) \), since \( \cos(\pi/3) = \tfrac12 \).
Combine the three features to match the correct description of the graph.

questions.stem: What is the amplitude, period and phase of \(f(x) = -2\cos(5x-\pi)\)?
options: Amplitude is 2, period is 5, phase shift is \(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\) to the right
Amplitude is \(-2\), period is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\), phase shift is \(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\) to the left
Amplitude is 2, period is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{5}\), phase shift is \(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\) to the right
Amplitude is 2, period is 5, phase shift is \(\pi\) to the left
questions.hint: Amplitude is always positive (take the magnitude of the leading coefficient); period \(=\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\) for \(\cos(nx-c)\); factor out \(n\) to find the phase shift.

steps.explain: Amplitude is the magnitude of the coefficient in front of cosine — always taken as positive.
For \(\cos(nx)\), the period is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\). Here \(n=5\).
Rewrite the argument by factoring out 5 to find the horizontal shift: \(5x-\pi = 5\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)\), which is a shift to the *right*.

questions.stem: The function \(y = 2\sin x + 1\) is translated up \(m\) units and then vertically dilated by a factor of \(n\) from the \(x\)-axis, where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive numbers. What is the range of the new curve?

steps.explain: The original curve \(y=2\sin x+1\) has range \([1-2, 1+2] = [-1, 3]\), since \(\sin x\) ranges over \([-1,1]\).
Translating up \(m\) units adds \(m\) to every value in the range.
A vertical dilation by factor \(n\) from the \(x\)-axis multiplies every \(y\)-value (and hence every range endpoint) by \(n\).
Expand the brackets.
